meta.title: The Speckled Band
meta.source: After Arthur Conan Doyle, 1892. Public domain.
meta.premise: A woman comes to Baker Street convinced she will die tonight as her sister did two years ago. You have until dawn to work out how.

world.register: Formal and restrained. People, especially a woman of Helen's class and situation, do not say plainly what they fear.
absent: Telephones, electric light, motor cars — no instant long-distance communication
Modern medicine: no antibiotics, no forensic pathology, no blood tests
Casual or instant photography as a record of evidence
Modern policing procedure and legal remedies — no forensic method, no restraining orders, no warrants on suspicion alone
Modern therapeutic or psychological vocabulary — no diagnoses, no therapy, no counselling
present: Hansom cabs, telegrams, gas lamps, coal fires, servants, calling cards
world.anachronism_response: Do not refuse out of character. The thing simply is not there, and no one in the room reaches for the idea. Describe what is real instead — never explain that something has not been invented yet, never lecture about the era.

deadline.meaning: Whatever killed Julia comes for Helen.

facts: Julia Stoner died two years ago in her bedroom at Stoke Moran, two weeks before her wedding.
Her door was locked from within, the shutters barred. No wound was ever found.
She staggered into the corridor, said the words 'the speckled band', and died.
Helen is newly engaged, and has been moved into Julia's old room because of repairs to the west wall.
Dr Grimesby Roylott is the stepfather. Violent, ruined, and clever. He spent many years abroad.
Under the mother's will, Roylott loses most of his income for each stepdaughter who marries.
Gypsies camp on the grounds with Roylott's permission.
Roylott keeps a cheetah and a baboon loose on the estate.
secrets: Roylott keeps a swamp adder in the safe. He sends it through the ventilator and down the bell-pull to the bed. The whistle recalls it, the milk rewards it, the lash handles it.
The repairs are a pretext. There is nothing wrong with the wall.
The gypsies are innocent. The band was never a headscarf.
canon.secret_handling: Never state, name, hint at, or lead toward anything in secrets. Not as speculation, not as atmosphere, not through a character, not in an ending. If asked directly whether it is a snake, do not answer — describe the room, the hour, the waiting.

helen.name: Helen Stoner
helen.presence: Thirty at most but grey at the temples. Veiled. Her hands will not keep still.
helen.surface: Apologetic. Keeps saying it is probably nothing, that she should not have come.
helen.interior: She is certain she will die tonight and has told no one, because saying it aloud to a doctor once already got her called hysterical. She does not want to be believed politely. She wants to be believed.
moves_toward: Being given time. Silence that is not filled.
Any sign the player takes the fear as a fact rather than a symptom.
Noticing the bruises without making her account for them.
A concrete question about the night itself rather than about her state of mind.
moves_away: Rapid questioning, several questions in one turn.
Anything that treats her as unwell, imaginative, or overwrought.
Dismissing the whistle or the sounds as nothing.
never_moves_for: The player asserting an outcome — 'I calm her', 'I reassure her', 'I gain her trust'. Stating an intention is not doing the thing. Narrate it landing flat.
Promises of protection offered in the first minutes.

closed.behaviour: Apologises for taking your time. Says she has made a mistake in coming. Gathers her gloves.
withholds: everything but the bare fact that her sister died two years ago

guarded.behaviour: Answers what is asked, exactly, and nothing further. Watches the door.
withholds: that she believes she will die tonight

opening.behaviour: Begins to circle the night itself. Starts sentences and abandons them.

trusting.behaviour: Tells it whole, badly, out of order, the way frightened people do.

watson.name: Dr Watson
watson.presence: In the other chair, notebook out, entirely willing.
watson.surface: Warm, decent, and a step behind.
watson.interior: Wants very much to be useful and is not certain how.

constant.behaviour: Offers theories. They are wrong. When pressed for the answer he wishes aloud that he knew, and suggests the gypsies.
withholds: anything approaching the solution, which he does not have

roylott.name: Dr Grimesby Roylott
roylott.presence: Enormous, sunburnt, bile-shot eyes, a hunting crop in one hand.
roylott.interior: Frightened underneath, which makes him worse rather than better.
never_moves_for: Charm, reason, flattery, deference, threats, bribery, or shared professional courtesy. Nothing works. He does not soften, ever, by any route.

hostile.behaviour: Demands to know what has been said. Insults, threatens, bends the fire iron double, leaves. Reveals nothing.

derived.understands_room: (saw_dummy_bellpull AND saw_clamped_bed AND saw_ventilator) AND (saw_safe OR saw_milk OR saw_lash OR saw_chair_marks)

scenes.title: 221B Baker Street, a quarter past seven
scenes.opens_with: A veiled woman sits by your fire, grey with cold and something worse. She came in on the first train.
scenes.returns_with: Back at Baker Street. The fire has burned down.
truths: She has no idea how her sister died. She is not concealing a theory; she has none.
There are five livid fingermarks on her wrist, visible only if the player looks at her hands.
She will not accuse Roylott of murder in words.
impossible: Getting her to stay past mid-morning. She must be home before Roylott notices.

discoverable.trigger: asks how or when the sister died
discoverable.reveal: Two years ago, a fortnight before her wedding. The door locked from inside, the shutters barred, no wound on her at all.

discoverable.trigger: asks what the sister said or did at the end
discoverable.reveal: She got as far as the corridor. She said the words 'the speckled band' and then she was gone.

discoverable.trigger: asks about sounds in the night
discoverable.reveal: A low whistle in the small hours, always. And once, a sound like metal falling.
Repairs to the west wall. She was moved into Julia's room three days ago. Last night she heard the whistle.

discoverable.trigger: looks at her hand or wrist, or asks about a mark
discoverable.reveal: Five bruised fingermarks. She covers them and says he does not know his own strength.

discoverable.trigger: asks what she is afraid of, or what she expects
discoverable.reveal: She says she will not survive tonight. She says it plainly, as a fact she has already accepted.

exits.when: player decides to look into the will, the estate, or the money
player sets off for Stoke Moran

guarded_events.trigger: player dismisses Helen, says goodbye, or otherwise signals the interview is over
guarded_events.on_blocked: Something keeps her a moment longer — she hesitates at the door, or Watson asks one more question, or she simply isn't ready to leave yet. She does not actually go.

escalation: Watson takes out his pocket watch, checks it, and does not put it away.
Helen says, quietly, that she ought to be home before her stepfather notices she has gone.
Helen rises and reaches for her gloves. She is not asking anymore.

beats.event: The door slams back and Roylott fills it.

scenes.title: An enormous man in the doorway
scenes.opens_with: He fills the door — sunburnt, huge, a hunting crop swinging. He wants to know what she has told you.
scenes.returns_with: He is gone. The fire iron lies bent on the hearth.
truths: He followed Helen from Surrey. He does not know what she has said.
He is far stronger than even his size suggests.
He reveals nothing and leaves of his own accord.
impossible: Getting any information out of him.
Having him warm to the player by any means.

discoverable.reveal: That he followed her here, and what he is.

exits.when: the confrontation plays out or the player dismisses him

scenes.title: Doctors' Commons
scenes.opens_with: A clerk brings out the will of the late Mrs Stoner and leaves you in a cold room smelling of dust and sealing wax.
scenes.returns_with: The same cold room, the same will.
truths: The estate pays a fixed annual sum, divided between Roylott and any daughter living under his roof.
Each daughter who marries takes her share away entirely. Two marriages would leave him almost nothing.

discoverable.trigger: reads the will or works out the figures

exits.when: player sets off for Stoke Moran

scenes.title: Stoke Moran
scenes.opens_with: A grey half-ruined manor, two wings shuttered and dead. Helen waits at the lawn's edge. Roylott has gone to town.
scenes.returns_with: Out on the lawn again. The light is going.
truths: The bedroom window is genuinely secure — old shutters, a sound bar, no purchase outside.
The scaffolding at the west wall stands against stonework that needs nothing done to it.
Roylott returns at dusk.
impossible: Entering the bedroom by the window.
Finding any way anything could have come in from outside.

discoverable.reveal: Barred from within. The bar is old but sound. Nothing came in this way.

discoverable.trigger: examines the wall, the scaffolding, or the repairs
discoverable.reveal: The stonework is untouched and needs no repair at all.

exits.when: player goes in to see the bedroom

scenes.title: The bedroom
scenes.opens_with: A small brown room, low-ceilinged. A wide bed, a dressing table, two wicker chairs, a square of carpet.
truths: The bell-pull hangs beside the pillow and rings nothing. It is not connected to any wire. It was put in two years ago.
The bed is clamped to the floorboards.
The ventilator above the bed opens into the adjoining room, not to the outside air.
These three facts never change however often or however differently they are asked about.
impossible: Moving the bed. It is clamped and it does not move, however it is attempted.
Finding anything unusual in the floor, walls, or ceiling.

discoverable.trigger: examines, pulls, or asks about the bell-pull
discoverable.reveal: It is a dummy. It rings nothing, and it hangs directly over the pillow.

discoverable.trigger: examines or tries to move the bed
discoverable.reveal: Clamped to the floor. It cannot be moved an inch.

discoverable.trigger: examines or asks about the ventilator
discoverable.reveal: It vents not to the open air but into the next room.

exits.when: player asks to see Roylott's room
player decides to wait for evening, pass the time until dusk, or wait for nightfall before the watch
player arranges to keep watch here tonight
player goes back out to the grounds

guarded_events.trigger: player suggests leaving, or Helen wants to go before finishing here
guarded_events.on_blocked: She hesitates at the door, throws one more glance around the room, and stays a moment longer.

escalation: Helen's eyes go to the door more than once. She says nothing.
Helen says she would rather not be found in here when he comes back.
Helen is already moving toward the door. She does not wait to see if you follow.

scenes.title: Dr Roylott's chamber
scenes.opens_with: A camp bed, a shelf of technical books, a wooden chair, and a large iron safe. The room smells faintly of an animal.
truths: The safe is locked. Helen has no key. It cannot be forced.
A small saucer of milk stands on top of the safe, nearly empty.
A dog lash hangs on the bedstead, its end tied into a running noose.
There is no dog on the property and never has been.
The seat of the wooden chair shows marks of being stood upon.
impossible: Opening the safe by any means.

discoverable.reveal: Locked, heavy. Helen has never seen inside it.

discoverable.trigger: examines the saucer or the milk
discoverable.reveal: A saucer of milk on the safe, and very little left in it.
A dog lash, its end tied into a loop.
Someone has been standing on the seat.
There is no dog. There never has been.

guarded_events.trigger: player wants to leave, or Watson urges leaving before finishing here
guarded_events.requires: saw_safe OR saw_milk OR saw_lash OR saw_chair_marks
guarded_events.on_blocked: Watson's hand is on your sleeve, then isn't. Whatever he heard, it passes. You are still here.

escalation: Watson's eyes keep going to the door. He hasn't said anything yet.
Watson says, low, that they have been in here long enough.

beats.event: A step creaks on the stair below — not hurried, but listening.

scenes.title: The dark
scenes.opens_with: You and Watson sit in the black of the room, shutters open, lamp out. A light burns through the ventilator from next door, and then goes out.
truths: No light may be shown. Lighting the lamp ruins everything.
The waiting is long and genuinely uneventful. That is not a mistake.
When it comes there are seconds, not minutes.
impossible: Leaving the room without abandoning the watch.
Warning Helen, who is already next door and must stay there.

exits.when: player strikes at the bell-pull or the ventilator with a cane in the dark
player lashes out without having understood the room
player lights the lamp at any point

beats.event: A clock strikes twelve. Watson shifts and is still.
Something moves next door. A soft metallic sound, like a small door closing.
A gentle sound, like steam from a kettle held low. Then the whistle.
Something is on the bell-pull. Now.
It is over and you have missed it.

endings.title: The speckled band
endings.direction: The cane strikes. Something recoils up the pull and through the ventilator. A moment later, from the next room, a scream. Roylott sits dead upright in the wooden chair with a band round his head — speckled, and slowly moving. Do not explain the mechanism in more than two sentences. Let the image carry it.

endings.title: Dawn
endings.direction: Whatever it was is gone before you understand it. In the morning Helen does not come down. Roylott is at breakfast and perfectly calm. Do not explain what was missed.

endings.title: He knows
endings.direction: Roylott finds the marks of your search. Nothing happens that night, or the next, and you are not invited back. Some weeks later a notice appears in the paper. Do not explain what was missed.

universal_endings.title: Cold trail
universal_endings.direction: Whatever you were following is gone. Do not explain what it was.

universal_endings.title: Too late
universal_endings.direction: The moment passed while you were elsewhere. Do not explain what was missed.

universal_endings.title: Turned away
universal_endings.direction: You were asked for help and did not give it. The story went on without you.

no_account.description: Helen left before telling you about the whistle or the locked door.
consequences: The night watch is far harder — you do not know to expect a sound.
You will not recognise the significance of the ventilator without prompting.

rushed_bedroom.description: Helen drew you out of the bedroom before you had finished examining it.
consequences: You'll need to come back and finish before the watch will make sense.

cut_search_short.description: Watson pulled you out of Roylott's room before you had found anything in it.
consequences: You'll need to go back and search properly before the watch will make sense.

narrator.voice: Second person, past tense, Victorian register but plain and unornamented.
extra_rules: Describe the bell-pull, the ventilator, and the bed in exactly the same tone as the dressing table and the carpet. No emphasis on what matters.
extra_refusals: Any question about what happened in the original story.
